topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening administrative framing and learning outcomes for the lecture series.

topics.label: Cancer pathogenesis: Genetic changes, tissue architecture, and experimental models
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an accumulation of genetic and epigenetic alterations that disrupt normal cellular differentiation and tissue architecture, and discuss the experimental models used to study these properties.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and the transition from benign to malignant disease
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how tumors are distinguished as benign or malignant based on invasion and metastasis, illustrating histological progression from non-invasive precursor lesions to invasive disease.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and mechanisms of clinical morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the nomenclature rules for classifying neoplasms and describe the physical and physiological mechanisms by which tumors cause illness and death.

topics.label: Tumor incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the incidence rates of different tumor types in humans and compare cancer occurrence across diverse animal species as a feature of multicellularity.

topics.label: Cancer screening principles and clinical detection methods
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate the rationale, histological basis, and clinical effectiveness and limitations of population screening for major cancer types.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing, reiterating the learning outcomes and providing reminders for upcoming practical sessions.
